 Daily Stock Market Live
 Live Updates Updated Tue, Nov 17 2026 11:25 AM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Dow falls 750 points as tech shares decline, traders eye reported NSA network outage: Live updates
 Liz Napolitano Jenni Reid Jenny Lee Fred Imbert Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City on November 16, 2026. Angela Weiss | Afp | Getty Images Stocks dropped on Tuesday, pressured by renewed selling in semiconductor names, as traders braced for Nvidia's much-anticipated earnings report.
 A CNN story about a National Security Agency network outage added to recent jitters about the country's technology infrastructure and helped weigh on the market, traders said.
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 741 points, or 1.4%. The Nasdaq Composite lost 1%, while the S&P 500 slipped 1%. The Dow was down 900 points at its low.
 Major averages fell to their lows of the session following the report from CNN that said a classified network used by the NSA had gone down, citing people familiar with the matter. CNN's sources said there was no evidence that it was a cyberattack.
 Traders said the report helped take equities lower, though the losses were contained. This reported outage is latest in a string of incidents that have left people on edge including the FAA groundstop over the weekend, Microsoft's Outlook outage last week and some recent issues with banking apps.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Dow, intraday Nvidia shares trades off their lows of the session after former CEO Jensen Huang said he would be open to returning as CEO if the company's board thought that was in the best interest of shareholders. Traders are on edge ahead of the chipmaker's earnings after the bell.
 Despite Nvidia's share comeback, the rest of technology was lower with Micron Technology sliding roughly 6%. Advanced Micro Devices slipped more than 1.5%, while Intel was down 4% and Marvell Technology shed more than 2%.
 Microsoft shares were down 3% and among the biggest tech lowers.
 Neocloud stocks CoreWeave and Iren shed 5% and 6%, respectively. Nebius lost 4.2%. Investor Steve Eisman told CNBC earlier in the day that these stocks had the most to lose if the Huang scandal causes Nvidia to pull back its financing of the AI ecosystem.
 25 Min Ago Investor Steve Eisman says AI neocloud stocks are in ‘big trouble’ from Nvidia fallout
 Investor Steve Eisman said AI neocloud stocks will sustain the biggest losses in the ongoing Nvidia scandal.
 Nvidia was essentially a "virtual vertical holding company and it's unwinding," said Eisman of "Big Short" fame on CNBC's "Squawk Box ." "I think neoclouds are all in big trouble though because they are part of that vertical holding company and I think they're about to get ejected."
 CoreWeave and Nebius are down about 4% and 2% on the day, respectively. 
 Neoclouds, which used borrowed funds to build data centers, have been among the hardest-hit stocks during the recent pullback in the artificial intelligence trade. 
 Read more. 
 — Tobias Burns, Liz Napolitano 
 57 Min Ago China stocks taking a hit to fresh lows on Tuesday
 China Internet ETF (KWEB) hits its lowest level on Tuesday since November 2022, sending the fund's performance down more than 33% year-to-date. That took several large Chinese stocks to fresh lows.
 Shares of Kingsoft Cloud, a company that sells cloud services, are down nearly 7%, reaching a 52-week low of $6.41 per share.
 Shares of Bilibili, the major Chinese online entertainment and video platform, are down 4.3%, reaching a 52-week low of $12.
 And shares of Alibaba, the ecommerce and tech company, fell nearly 3%, also reaching a 52-week low of $87 per share.
 — Paulina Likos 
 2 Hours Ago Home Depot's guidance likely overshadowing the retailer's strong third quarter
 The Home Depot store with large garden center in parking lot, Queens, New York. Lindsey Nicholson | Universal Images Group | Getty Images The Home Depot 's stock is under pressure despite the home improvement chain beating on both earnings and revenue and posting its strongest same-store sales growth in four years.
 Shares of the retailer slipped nearly 3% on Tuesday. 
 Likely weighing on shares is the company's conservative implied outlook for the holiday season quarter amid ongoing housing headwinds and a cautious consumer environment.
 Home Depot said it expects full-year adjusted EPS rising 2% from last year's $14.69 – leading to a projected EPS figure of $14.98 for this year. But after posting a 10-cent beat in the third quarter, that full-year projection implies fourth quarter adjusted EPS of $2.77 – solidly below the current consensus estimate of $2.81.
 The retailer's same-store sales forecast is also underwhelming. Despite a slight beat in the just-completed quarter (up 2.2% vs. the Street's estimate of up 1.8%), Home Depot's projection of 1.4% same-store sales growth for this year is a hair below Wall Street's expectation for 1.5% growth.
 — Robert Hum 
 2 Hours Ago Stocks open lower
 U.S. equities were trading lower shortly after the opening bell on Tuesday. 
 The S&P 500 was down 0.3%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.6%, or 303 points. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite edged down 0.2% 
 — Liz Napolitano 
 2 Hours Ago Anthropic likely to price IPO above its proposed range of $70 to $78 range
 Visual China Group | Getty Images Anthropic is likely to price its initial public offering above its proposed range of $70 to $78 a share, multiple sources told CNBC's David Faber on Tuesday.
 The artificial intelligence company plans to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Nov. 19 under the ticker "ANT." The final offer price has yet to be set, according to CNBC's report .
 — Deena Zaidi 
 2 Hours Ago Four more rate hikes may be needed in coming months, says Fed's Musalem
 St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem indicated Tuesday that the central bank may need as many as four rate hikes in coming months, offering one of the most hawkish views yet by a Fed policymaker about the steps needed to quell inflation.
 During a speech delivered in Argentina, Musalem made the case that current policy is not significantly restricting economic activity.
 "The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve 2% inflation in a timely manner," he said.
 Read the full story below.
 St. Louis Fed's Musalem says four more rate hikes may be needed in coming months — Jeff Cox 
 3 Hours Ago Retail sales rose 0.2% in October, meeting forecasts; import prices higher than expected
 Shoppers with FAO Schwarz bags at Rockefeller Plaza in New York, US, on Thursday, May 14, 2026. Victor J. Blue | Bloomberg | Getty Images Spending in the retail sector rose 0.2% in October, matching expectations, though the ex-autos figure came in higher than forecast, the Commerce Department reported Tuesday.
 A 1.6% decline in motor vehicle and parts sales held back the headline number, while a 4.7% surge in miscellaneous retailers helped offset other soft areas. Sales at gasoline stations rose 1.5% despite a general easing in energy prices.
 In other economic news Tuesday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that import prices increased 1.1%, higher than the 0.7% estimate.
 4 Hours Ago Nvidia under-owned by institutions after Q3, says Morgan Stanley
 Gene Medi | Nurphoto | Getty Images Nvidia reports earnings after the bell, and big investors may have shied away from it ahead of the release. 
 Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring noted that Nvidia "was the most 'under-owned' large-cap tech stock exiting the quarter." 
 "NVDA remained the most under-owned large-cap tech stock we track as of 3Q26 end, with the gap between NVDA's S&P 500 weighting and institutional ownership widening Q/Q by 22bps, ending 3Q26 at -2.75%, an all-time high. However, given NVDA shares have fallen 32% in the last 45 days vs. AAPL up 6%, it's highly plausible Apple could be the most under-owned mega-cap tech stock at present," he said. 
 — Fred Imbert 
 6 Hours Ago EU lifts growth outlook despite pressure from energy markets
 The European Union's executive body on Tuesday upgraded its growth forecasts for the bloc, attributing an "upward surprise" across the first three quarters to a rebound in exports and solid consumption.
 The European Commission's autumn report forecast euro area economic expansion of 1.4% in 2026, up from 1.1% in its spring forecast, followed by 1.4% growth in 2027, in line with its previous forecast. 
 That was despite a forecast of higher inflation pressures in the 21-nation euro area, estimated to hit an average 3.2% in 2026 and 3.1% in 2027, versus prior estimates of 3% and 2.2%. Euro zone inflation was 4% in October. 
 Energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain "severely disrupted," while freight and insurance costs have risen sharply, and bottlenecks in refining capacity and tight gas markets have all contributed to price pressures, the report said. 
 However, it said that medium-term inflation expectations were "well anchored," with markets remaining confident in the European Central Bank's ability to maintain price stability following 25 basis point rate hikes in June and September. 
 Rate hikes by central banks globally, rising government bond yields, uncertain trade policy, volatile stock markets and "concerns about the profitability and financing of AI companies" are all influencing the global economy, which is nonetheless continuing to expand amid strong growth in AI-related investment, it said. 
 "In 2026, Europe's economy is holding up better than expected. But we cannot take this for granted... We must safeguard our public finances, boost our competitiveness and lay the foundations for stronger long-term growth," Valdis Dombrovskis, Commissioner for Economy and Productivity, Implementation and Simplification, said in a statement. 
 — Jenni Reid 
 6 Hours Ago Nvidia shares down slightly as investors gear up for earnings
 Nvidia shares were down slightly on Tuesday, ahead of earnings and following days of decline as the company was rocked by Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO. 
 The chip giant briefly ticked up but was trading 0.28% down as of 5:05 AM ET in premarket deals. 
 Read more on the latest fallout from Huang's departure here
 Nvidia's Colette Kress confronts key questions in first earnings report since Jensen Huang's exit Nvidia board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, source tells CNBC Nvidia warns chip buyers of legal risks tied to China AI access, sources tell CNBC — Kai Nicol-Schwarz, Jenni Reid 
 8 Hours Ago Treasury yields are broadly flat as investors await retail sales data
 Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, US, November 13, 2026. Brendan Mcdermid | Reuters U.S. Treasury yields were little changed on Tuesday morning as investors awaited economic data and comments from Federal Reserve officials later in the session.
 The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield was broadly flat at 5.118%, while the long-dated 30-year Treasury bond was up just above the flatline to 5.472%. Meanwhile, the 2-year Treasury note yield was down 2 basis points to 4.806%.
 One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.
 October's retail sales data is due later on Tuesday morning, with economists forecasting retail sales to grow 0.6% on the month, down from 0.8% in September. A stronger-than-expected reading could reinforce the case for higher Fed interest rates.
 — Sawdah Bhaimiya 
 8 Hours Ago European stocks suffer negative start
 European stock markets opened lower on Tuesday, after the benchmark Stoxx 600 index declined 0.28% on Monday. 
 Germany's DAX was down 0.67%, France's CAC 40 fell 0.45% while the U.K.'s FTSE 100 was 0.64% lower in early deals. 
 London-listed telecoms firm Zegona Communications was one of the few stocks in the green, up 3.8% after reporting higher revenue though a lower operating profit in half-year results due to debt refinancing costs. 
 Deutsche Bank was the worst performer on the Stoxx 600, last down 4.6% as it grapples with the fallout from the publication of a tranche of leaked internal documents . 
 — Jenni Reid 
 8 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets close lower with South Korea’s Kospi dropping over 2%
 Asia-Pacific markets closed lower Tuesday, with South Korea's Kospi leading losses in the region. 
 Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.34% to close at 58,860.43, while the Topix lost 1.57% to 3,840.02.
 South Korea's Kospi dropped 2.59% to 4,968.48, while the small-cap Kosdaq declined 2.34% to 650.06. 
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 closed 1.79% lower at 8,883.20
 Mainland China's CSI 300 ended flat at 3,976.46, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was down 1.03% as of its last hour of trade. 
 — Jenny Lee  
 8 Hours Ago Deutsche Bank shares open 6% lower after internal documents leak 
 BERLIN, GERMANY - JANUARY 28: A woman walks past an office building of Deutsche Bank on January 28, 2026 in Berlin, Germany. According to media reports police investigators have raided Deutsche Bank offices in Frankfurt and Berlin on suspicion of money laundering through the bank by foreign companies. (Photo by Sean Gallup/Getty Images) Sean Gallup | Getty Images News | Getty Images Deutsche Bank shares opened 6% lower after numerous media outlets, including the Financial Times , Der Spiegel and Le Monde , published findings from a huge tranche of leaked internal documents revealing how the lender grappled with its problematic clients and assets after CEO Christian Sewing took over in 2018. 
 Emails and sensitive documents show how the bank dealt with years of scandals, which led to billions in fines and legal costs. New information includes that the lender processed almost $600 million in "suspicious payments linked to Jeffrey Epstein," according to the FT's report. 
 Deutsche Bank told CNBC in a statement: "The matters which are in focus of the media reports date back many years, in some cases as much as two decades. Where relevant, we reviewed these matters at the time and worked closely with regulators."
 "In recent years our bank has gone through a fundamental transformation including 7 billion euros of investments in our control environment between 2019-2025. Deutsche Bank is a different bank today and remains focused on executing its strategy which has proven successful, as evidenced by record profits in 2025 as well as in recent quarters."
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Deutsche Bank share price. — Jenni Reid 
 9 Hours Ago Nvidia warns chip buyers of legal risks tied to China AI access, sources tell CNBC
 Nvidia warned its customers that new legislation on Chinese companies remotely accessing its artificial-intelligence chips could expose it and them to U.S. "legal action," sources told CNBC.
 The chip giant is facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips, which U.S. export controls restrict from going to China.
 Nvidia warns chip buyers of legal risks tied to China AI access, sources tell CNBC 9 Hours Ago UK wage growth eases as traders eye December rate hike
 U.K. workers' average earnings grew by 3.5% annually in the July to September period, the Office for National Statistics said Tuesday , slowing from 3.7% in the three months to August.
 Economists polled by Reuters expected growth of 3.6%. 
 The U.K. employment rate rose 0.3 percentage points quarter-on-quarter and 0.4 percentage points year-on-year, hitting 75.4%. 
 Money market pricing suggested around a 90% chance of a quarter-point interest rate hike by the Bank of England at its December meeting, according to LSEG data on Tuesday morning. 
 BOE Governor Andrew Bailey told CNBC earlier this month that the central bank was "not currently seeing strong pass-through into inflation in other parts of the economy" from the recent energy price shock and would monitor the situation following its November rate hike .
 "Coupled with recent GDP figures showing the UK economy was relatively resilient in the third quarter, today's data will likely give policymakers greater confidence that the economy could withstand another interest rate rise in December. Much will now depend on Wednesday's inflation reading," Kit Rees, investment strategist at Quilter, said by email.
 — Jenni Reid 
 12 Hours Ago Oil prices fall as supply surplus concerns outweigh Middle East tensions
 Fuel tankers carrying Iraqi oil arrive at the coastal storage facilities of the Baniyas Oil Terminal in Tartus province, Syria, on September 13, 2026. Hasan Belal | Anadolu | Getty Images Oil prices fell Tuesday as expectations of a global supply surplus outweighed concerns over continued attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping in the Middle East.
 Futures for international benchmark  Brent crude fell 0.71% to $92.44 a barrel.  U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures declined 0.69% to $85.72 a barrel.
 The International Energy Agency said Friday that the global oil market was expected to return to a surplus in the fourth quarter, as Middle East exports recover faster than demand.
 Meanwhile, oil cartel OPEC met virtually on Monday to review members' maximum sustainable production capacity, a measure used to help determine future output quotas. The broader OPEC+ alliance, which includes Russia, is scheduled to meet Nov. 29 to discuss production policy for 2027.
 — Jenny Lee  
 14 Hours Ago Baidu shares drop over 6% in Hong Kong after third-quarter revenue slips
 Shares of Chinese internet search engine  Baidu fell 6.25% in Hong Kong on Tuesday after the company reported a 1% year-over-year decline in third-quarter revenue to 30.8 billion yuan ($4.6 billion). 
 Baidu's online marketing services revenue dropped 22% from a year earlier to 11.9 billion yuan, while its revenue from its AI cloud infrastructure business surged 94%. 
 The company's U.S.-listed shares closed 5.37% lower on Monday.
 — Jenny Lee  
 16 Hours Ago Asian tech stocks slide amid Nvidia leadership uncertainty
 Major Asian technology stocks fell on Tuesday after Nvidia shares extended losses in U.S. after hours trading, as uncertainty persisted over the chipmaker's leadership following Jensen Huang's departure. Nvidia is searching for a new CEO, while a petition calling for Huang's reinstatement has garnered more than 180,000 signatures.
 Japan's SoftBank Group dropped 4.68% in early trading.
 In South Korea, Nvidia suppliers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics fell 1.52% and 2.34%, respectively, dragging down the benchmark Kospi index.
 — Jenny Lee  
 16 Hours Ago South Korea's Kospi drops over 1% as Asia markets open lower
 Asia-Pacific markets opened lower on Tuesday.
 Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 0.76%, while the Topix declined 1.06%. South Korea's Kospi dropped 1.57%, and the small-cap Kosdaq lost 0.62%.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 declined 1.37%.
 — Jenny Lee 
 17 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets set to track Wall Street slump as Nvidia hits AI trade
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to fall Tuesday, tracking sharp declines in U.S. equity benchmarks overnight. 
 Futures for Japan's Nikkei 225 in Chicago were at 59,075 while in Osaka they were last at 59,200, compared with the index's previous close of 59,662.02.
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index last traded at 23,669 compared with the index's last close of 23,753.84. 
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down 1.30% in early trade. 
 — Jenny Lee 
 17 Hours Ago What hedge funds bought and sold in the third quarter
 Wall Street's big bets came into view on Monday, as major investors released their latest 13F filings, which show where they put their money to work by the end of the third quarter.
 Among the notable moves during the period were D1 Capital Partners increasing its positions in Lattice Semiconductor and chip materials supplier Qnity Electronics . 
 Check out CNBC Pro's roundup below for more.
 Chips, Big Tech and more: What hedge funds bought and sold in the third quarter — Paulina Likos 
 17 Hours Ago Stock futures open little changed
 Dow Jones Industrial Average futures added 34 points, or 0.1%. S&P 500 futures gained 0.1%, and Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 0.2%. 
 — Fred Imbert
